_readme: placements.json: every placement the tool knows, and what each one ACCEPTS (copied from its spec sheet).
The tool works out the files itself: placements whose rules overlap share one file. There is nothing to group by hand.
To add a placement, copy one entry, change it to match the new spec sheet, then open check.html to see which file it joins.

encoding._note: Defaults used when a placement does not say otherwise. videoKbps is the quality aimed for; it is moved inside each file's allowed range automatically.

strictness._note: How the report decides PASS / WARN / FAIL. Loudness within loudnessPassDb of target = PASS, within loudnessWarnDb = WARN, else FAIL. A frame counts as a duplicate when its average brightness differs from the previous frame by less than dupDiffThreshold (0 to 255 scale).

spotLengths._note: A video within snapWithinSec of one of these lengths (in seconds) is made exactly that long: cut if a little long, last frame held if a little short. Length is counted in frames, like broadcast timecode (6 s = 180 frames at 29.97 fps).

limits._note: Browser memory guard. Based on ONE test point (a 526 MB ProRes output worked, using about 2.3 GB of browser memory). Adjust after more testing.

grain._note: Light grain (temporal noise) that stops exact duplicate frames. OFF by default; the page offers it when the frame rate is changed or the check finds repeated frames. Tested 2026-11-09: strength 1 changes nothing, 3 and 5 are unreliable, 4 removed every exact repeat at 6 to 20 Mbps H.264 and ProRes. Use even numbers. Raised to 6 on 2026-11-18: the browser encoder (single-threaded) left 1 repeat in 179 frames at 4 on a frame-rate-converted clip; 6 left none there and none in 449 frames of a 15 s converted spot. A preset can override with "noise": {"strength": 6}.

placements.name: Cineplex: cinema pre-show

source.label: Cineplex Media Digital Pre-Show specs, dated May 9, 2024 (PDF supplied by team). Received Nov 10, 2026 and confirmed against the tool that day.

naming.note: Max 12 characters before the extension, letters and numbers only, end with a language letter.

notes: Confirmed Nov 10, 2026 against the spec sheet received that day (Cineplex Media Digital Pre-Show specs, dated May 9, 2024).
Audio: the written rule is used (average no higher than -12 dB, peaks no higher than -8 dB). The '-10db' in the spec table is not treated as a target.
File names: max 12 characters, no special characters, end with a language letter (E = English, F = French), for example NAMEE.MOV. Type the name yourself.
Text-safe area is 1724 x 972. Video files only, no stills.
Sound: Cineplex sets limits, not a target: average no higher than -12 dB, peaks no higher than -8 dB. Quieter audio is left as it is; louder audio is turned down.

The sheet says the QuickTime info must read "Apple ProRes/Apple ProRes HQ", so ProRes 422 and ProRes 422 HQ are both accepted. This tool makes ProRes 422 (about 30% smaller, about 550 MB for 30 s); a ProRes 422 HQ video is already good to go. The sheet also says 8-bit; ProRes is 10-bit, which is standard.

placements.name: Rogers Sports & Media: digital video

source.label: Rogers Sports & Media ad specifications, Digital Video (web page, no date shown). Pulled from the official online source; confirmed against the tool Nov 17, 2026. The RSM Ad Manager self-serve help pages could not be reached online, so the self-serve limits (85 MB, up to 30 s) come from the specs the team supplied.

notes: Confirmed Nov 17, 2026 against the official Rogers Sports & Media web page (no date shown), pulled online. The self-serve RSM Ad Manager limits come from the specs the team supplied, as the help pages could not be reached.
One file that meets both Rogers specs: booked through a Rogers rep, and self-serve in RSM Ad Manager.
MP4, H.264, progressive, 1920 x 1080. A constant 18 Mbps: inside the 10 to 40 Mbps range, and a 30 second spot (about 70 MB) stays under the self-serve limit of 85 MB.
23.976 or 29.97 fps (29.97 preferred).
No duplicate frames allowed. No slates or load plates.
Audio AAC, 192 kbps or higher, 48 kHz, stereo. Loudness -24 LKFS (plus or minus 2), true peak no higher than -1 dB.
Self-serve takes spots up to 30 seconds; 60 second spots go through a rep, where there is no size limit.
Captions only through VAST 4.x, never burned in. Send 5 days before launch.
Sound: -24 LKFS with true peak no higher than -1 dB, per the Rogers spec.

placements.name: Crave / Bell Media: streaming and connected TV

tile.title: Crave / Bell
tile.sub: Streaming: Crave, CTV app, Noovo, TSN

source.label: Bell Media Digital Advertising Standards and Creative Specifications, last revised Oct 21, 2026 (PDF, Connected TV / VAST video specs). Pulled from the official online source; confirmed against the tool Nov 17, 2026.

notes: Confirmed Nov 17, 2026 against the official Bell Media spec PDF, last revised Oct 21, 2026, pulled online. Its video specs are unchanged from the April 16, 2026 version.
One spec covers Crave, CTV, Noovo, TSN, CP24, BNN and CTV News on connected TV ("Crave now includes CTV and Noovo").
MP4, H.264, progressive, 1920 x 1080 recommended (1280 x 720 minimum). 6, 15 or 30 seconds.
Max file size 25 MB, minimum 5,000 kbps. A 30 s spot must stay near 6 Mbps to fit, so this preset uses a constant 5,800 kbps (constant, so simple scenes do not drop under the minimum).
Frame rates 23.98, 29.97 or 59.94. Bell converts 23.98 to 29.97 on its side.
Audio AAC 44.1 kHz, -24 LKFS (plus or minus 2), average about -12 dB with nothing peaking over -9 dB.
Sound: -24 LKFS with peaks held under -9 dB, per the Bell spec.

placements.name: CTV: local TV stations

tile.title: CTV
tile.sub: Local TV stations (adds 10 s of black)

source.label: CTV local station commercial specs (Word document supplied by team; no date printed on the sheet). Received Nov 11, 2026 and confirmed against the tool that day.

naming.note: Use Client_SpotName_Duration_ProductionCompany, for example CAA_TravelInsurance_30_CAANEO. No spaces.

notes: Confirmed Nov 11, 2026 against the spec sheet received that day (CTV local station commercial specs; no date printed on the sheet).
Local CTV stations ask for at least 10 seconds of black after the commercial. This tile adds 10 seconds of black and silence after the spot is cut to its exact length.
Accepted: MOV, MP4 or AVI at 1920 x 1080, ProRes 4:2:2 or H.264. This preset makes an H.264 MP4 at a steady 20 Mbps.
Audio 48 kHz, stereo or mono mix (no split tracks). The sheet gives no loudness target, so the Canadian broadcast standard of -24 LKFS is used.
File name: Client_SpotName_Duration_ProductionCompany, for example CAA_TravelInsurance_30_CAANEO. Type it yourself.
Closed captions go as a separate .scc file. This tool does not make captions.
Upload at least 2 business days before the start date. Upload details are on the station's sheet; check with your CTV Account Executive.
Sound: Not on the CTV sheet. Uses the Canadian broadcast standard (-24 LKFS, peaks no higher than -2 dB).

placements.name: Corus: online video and connected TV

tile.title: Corus
tile.sub: Pre-roll and connected TV: StackTV, Pluto TV

source.label: Corus Digital Creative Specifications (PDF supplied by team; no date printed on the sheet), In-Stream, Pre-Roll and Connected TV video column. Received Nov 11, 2026 and confirmed against the tool that day.

notes: Confirmed Nov 11, 2026 against the spec sheet received that day (Corus Digital Creative Specifications; no date printed on the sheet).
Covers in-stream, pre-roll and connected TV (StackTV, Pluto TV). MP4 only: no MOV on Pluto TV.
MP4, H.264 with AAC audio, 1920 x 1080 recommended (1280 x 720 and 640 x 360 also accepted).
29.97 frames per second. A 23.976 video is converted to 29.97 by this preset.
Video bitrate 4,500 to 8,000 kbps; this preset uses a constant 6,000 kbps. Max file 510 MB. 6, 15 or 30 seconds.
Audio AAC 128 kbps, 48 kHz, stereo. The sheet gives no loudness target, so the sound is left as it is.
Send to Corus 5 business days before launch (10 if a third-party vendor is involved).
Sound: No loudness rule in the Corus spec sheet.

placements.name: Amazon Prime Video

source.label: Amazon Ads, Streaming TV and Prime Video ad specs (web page, no date shown). Pulled from the official online source; confirmed against the tool Nov 17, 2026.

notes: Confirmed Nov 17, 2026 against the official Amazon Ads web page (no date shown), pulled online.
At least 1920 x 1080. Frame rate 23.976 (recommended), 24, 25 or 29.97. Sound 44.1 or 48 kHz. MP4 only here; MOV is not on Amazon's list.
Canadian spots run 15, 30, 45 or 60 seconds.
Minimum 15 Mbps video and 192 kbps audio, max 500 MB, come from team notes. This preset targets 25 Mbps. Raise it if the placement asks for more, but watch the 500 MB limit.
Sound: No target known.

placements.name: Disney+

source.label: Disney+ Creative Details & Requirements, updated Aug 6, 2025 (RSM Streaming TV single ad spec; Disney+ in Canada is sold through Rogers Sports & Media). Received Nov 16, 2026 and confirmed against the tool that day.

safeZones.label: Player ad overlay, keep clear (220 x 135). From Disney's US guidance, not the Canadian sheet

notes: Confirmed Nov 16, 2026 against the spec sheet received that day (Disney+ Creative Details & Requirements, updated Aug 6, 2025). One deliberate difference: the tool accepts black bars, which the sheet does not allow.
23.976 fps accepted, 29.97 preferred. Keep the frame rate native: Disney rejects files with duplicate frames, which come from converting the frame rate.
Audio AAC, stereo, 48 kHz. Loudness -24 LKFS (plus or minus 2), peaks no higher than -1 dBTP.
Length must be exactly to the second (for example 15 or 30 seconds) or it is rejected.
No slates or load plates. The sheet also says no letterboxing or black bars; the tool lets bars through, so make sure they are intentional before sending.
AI used anywhere in the ad must be disclosed on screen (for example "Generated by AI"), easy to notice, at the start or end.
Send through RSM at least 5 business days before launch. RSM checks it first, then Disney+ approves it (3 to 5 business days in all). Updated files mid-campaign go to RSM first.
Ad Standards Canada clearance is needed for food and drink, alcohol, cosmetics, health products and anything aimed at children. Think TV approval is needed for gaming and betting.
Keep important content out of the top-right 220 x 135 px (player ad overlay). This comes from Disney's US guidance; the Canadian sheet does not mention it.

placements.name: Landmark Cinemas: pre-show

source.label: Landmark Cinemas Onscreen Advertising Specs & Delivery (rate card PDF supplied by team; no date printed on the sheet, the file name says 2023). Received Nov 11, 2026 and confirmed against the tool that day.

naming.note: Use LC-Client-SpotName-Duration-Language-Month, for example LC-CAA-TravelInsurance-30-ENG-Dec. No spaces.

notes: Confirmed Nov 11, 2026 against the spec sheet received that day (Landmark Cinemas Onscreen Advertising Specs & Delivery; no date printed on the sheet, the file name says 2023).
Digital motion ads: MP4, H.264, 50 Mbps or higher, 24 or 23.976 fps, 1920 x 1080. This preset uses a constant 55 Mbps so simple scenes do not drop under the minimum.
Audio: the sheet mentions uncompressed 48 kHz 16-bit WAV or AIFF; Landmark has confirmed that a separate WAV is not required. This preset puts high-quality AAC (320 kbps) inside the MP4.
Audio level: the sheet says average 'higher than -12' with peaks not over -8. Read as the same limits as Cineplex (average no higher than -12 dB, peaks no higher than -8 dB). Confirm with Landmark.
File name must follow LC-Client-SpotName-Duration-Language-Month, for example LC-CAA-TravelInsurance-30-ENG-Dec. Type it yourself.
Text-safe area is 1724 x 972. Deliver through Landmark's WeTransfer page (landmarkcinemas.wetransfer.com).
Showtime slides (2048 x 858 scope and 1998 x 1080 flat JPEGs) are still images, not covered by this tool.
Sound: Landmark sets limits: average no higher than -12 dB, peaks no higher than -8 dB. Quieter audio is left as it is; louder audio is turned down.

placements.name: Spotify video ad

source.label: Spotify Advertising, Video Takeover ad specs (web page, no date shown). Pulled from the official online source; confirmed against the tool Nov 17, 2026.

notes: Confirmed Nov 17, 2026 against the official Spotify Advertising web page (no date shown), pulled online.

9:16 or 16:9, NTSC or PAL frame rates, progressive (not interlaced). Audio is required (no silent files). Audio bitrate 198 to 320 kbps: Spotify has rejected files below 198 kbps, so this is checked. Corus needs exactly 128 kbps, so Spotify always gets its own file.
Spotify asks for no letterboxing, pillarboxing or slates. The tool flags black bars as a warning; make sure there are none before sending.
30 seconds or less, max 500 MB, at least about 720 px on the short side, from team notes.
Loudness: RMS -14 dBFS with peak -0.2 dBFS (Phase 2). RMS is not the same as LUFS; the tool will label which it measures.
Sound: RMS target, not LUFS.

placements.name: YouTube

source.label: YouTube Help, Recommended upload encoding settings (web page, no date shown). Pulled from the official online source; confirmed against the tool Nov 17, 2026.

notes: Confirmed Nov 17, 2026 against the official YouTube Help page on upload settings (no date shown), pulled online. Ad formats: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/17091270
MP4, no edit lists, moov atom at the front, H.264 High, progressive, 2 consecutive B-frames, closed GOP at half the frame rate, 4:2:0, BT.709, VBR, same frame rate as the source.
YouTube recommends about 8 Mbps for 1080p at 24 to 30 fps and 12 Mbps at 48 to 60 fps. These are recommendations, not minimums, so video bitrate is not checked. Files made here are well above them.
Audio: AAC-LC stereo, 48 or 96 kHz, 384 kbps recommended. Files made here use 48 kHz. Audio bitrate is not checked.
This tool does not deinterlace. Interlaced sources show a warning.
Covers YouTube ads: pre-roll (in-stream), in-feed and Shorts.
Sound: YouTube normalizes loudness itself.
ProRes uploads also work but are far larger, so this tool makes MP4.

placements.name: Meta: Facebook and Instagram

source.label: Meta Ads Guide, Facebook Feed and Instagram Reels video specs (web pages, no date shown). Instagram Reels: https://www.facebook.com/business/ads-guide/update/video/instagram-reels Pulled from the official online source; confirmed against the tool Nov 17, 2026.

notes: Confirmed Nov 17, 2026 against the official Meta Ads Guide pages (no date shown), pulled online.
MP4 or MOV, H.264, max 4 GB, fixed frame rate, progressive, no edit lists. Sound is optional; if present, AAC at 128 kbps or more.
Meta accepts small pictures (120 px wide for Feed, 500 px for Reels) but recommends at least 1080 px. Files made here are 1080 on the short side.
Covers Facebook and Instagram Feed, Reels and Stories ads. Safe zones are not documented here.

placements.name: Custom
notes: Pick the file type, frame rate, bitrate and sound yourself under "Change settings".
